workflows.name: > FortiEDR v2 > Fetch
workflows.description: Reads the last-pull-time watermark and reads the FortiEDR events whose activity (Last Seen, by default) falls inside the window since it. The first run, and any run after the macro was lost, reads the Initial Backfill Range instead.

arguments.last_pull_time: {% if vars.request.env_setup or not vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'] or vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'][0].value == '0' %}{% else %}{{ vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'][0].value }}{% endif %}
arguments.window_from: {% if vars.last_pull_time %}{{ vars.last_pull_time }}{% else %}{{ arrow.utcnow().shift(minutes=-(vars.fetch_last_minutes|int)).format('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss') }}{% endif %}

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Wizard-editable defaults. `fetch_last_minutes` is the backfill window
used while the watermark is missing or '0'. The macro name is scoped to
this playbook's UUID, so two ingestion configurations never share a
watermark. `max_events` fails a run whose window exceeds it -- the
window fetch is count-verified and never paged, so a partial read
must never advance the watermark.

groups.name: Note: Environment Setup
groups.description:
Runs when the watermark macro does not exist yet, not only on the
wizard's `vars.request.env_setup` first pass. It must come AFTER Get
Macro Value so its absence can be seen: Update Last Pull Time only
updates the macro, it does not create it, so a missing macro would
otherwise leave the watermark unwritten and every run would read the
backfill window again without any error.
The macro is primed to '0', which Set Time Configuration reads as a
cold start.

groups.name: Note: Set Time Configuration
groups.description:
`curr_timestamp` is the end of this run's window, 60 seconds behind the
clock (see the block comment above) and in the management API's native
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (UTC) format. It is written back to the macro only
after Ingest succeeds, so a failed run reads its window again.
`last_pull_time` is empty on a cold start (macro missing, or '0'); the
run then computes `window_from` as now minus `fetch_last_minutes`.

groups.name: Note: Ingest Events
groups.description:
The connector op pages through the events itself (up to Maximum Events
Per Run) and returns each one already mapped to an alert payload:
external_id = eventId, severity clamped to the Severity picklist,
process/device/destinations split into their own keys, and the raw
event kept in source_payload.

groups.name: Note: Save Result
groups.description:
The Fetch -> Ingest contract. Ingest reads every one of these back off
the workflow_reference step ("Fetch Events") as
`vars.steps.Fetch_Events.<key>`.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Ingest
workflows.description: Orchestrator: calls Fetch, then either returns a sample record for the wizard's Data Mapping preview (env_setup mode) or creates one alert per FortiEDR event and advances the last-pull-time watermark.

routes.name: Create Record -> Update Last Pull Time

groups.name: Note: Mapping Preview
groups.description:
The Data Ingestion Wizard runs the Ingest playbook with
`vars.request.env_setup == true` while the analyst designs the field
mapping in the UI. In that mode the first fetched record is returned so
the wizard can render the Data Mapping preview; no alerts are written.
`false` (or missing) is the real ingestion path.

groups.name: Note: Return Sample
groups.description:
The sample for the wizard's Data Mapping preview: the first mapped
event of the window, whose keys are the fields `Create Record` maps.
Falls back to a representative record when the window is empty, so the
preview still renders.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
The values the alerts take from the connector's output: the window's
mapped events and the macro holding its watermark.

groups.name: Note: Create Record
groups.description:
The step is named "Create Record" because the Data Ingestion Wizard's
Data Mapping page is shown only for a create playbook with a step of
exactly that name, and it reads the target module off this step.

`is_upsert` routes this at /api/3/upsert/alerts, keyed on sourceId (the
eventId). That is the dedup that makes the Last Seen window safe: a
window that is read twice, or an event re-triggered and fetched again,
updates its existing alert instead of duplicating it. Without it the
plain insert path 409s on the sourceId uniqueness constraint.

The connector already clamps severity and alert_type to picklist
members, so the picklist filters cannot fail with an unmapped value.
The date is the event's firstSeen epoch (alertDetectionDate), while
sourcedata keeps the whole mapped payload including last_observed_epoch
and the raw event.

`description` is passed WITHOUT the `| e` escape filter: the connector
builds it as sanitised rich text (inline styles only), and escaping it
here would store visible `<table>` markup instead of rendering the
card. This matches the FortiSIEM v2 ingestion playbook.

groups.name: Note: Update Last Pull Time
groups.description:
Advances the watermark only after the alerts are written, so a failed
Create Record leaves the window to be read again.

data.name: Sample - Fortinet FortiEDR v2 Use Cases - 1.1.0
data.description: Operational use-case playbooks for the "Fortinet FortiEDR v2" connector: alert triage with collector isolation, evidence collection, time-limited exception governance, a re-detection digest over console incidents, a file-hash IOC retro-hunt, and a fleet compliance audit. Clone before use, like every sample collection: the connector upgrade deletes and re-imports sample collections, so local edits are lost on upgrade.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Triage to Isolation
workflows.description: Record action on an ingested FortiEDR alert: refresh the event from the console, list the exceptions already muting it, collect the raw memory evidence, and -- with the analyst's approval -- isolate the collector. Approve and decline both land as comments on the alert.

message.content: Triage to Isolation: no FortiEDR event found for sourceId {{ vars.event_id }} -- investigate manually; the console may have archived or pruned this event.

steps.name: Isolation Approval
steps.description: FortiEDR event {{ vars.event_id }} -- {{ vars.severity }}, {{ vars.process }} first seen {{ vars.first_seen }}, last seen {{ vars.last_seen }}, already carrying {{ vars.steps.Check_Existing_Exceptions.data | default([]) | length }} exception rule(s). Isolation cuts {{ vars.device }} off from the network until a "Unisolate" call releases it.

schema.title: Approve collector isolation
schema.description: FortiEDR event {{ vars.event_id }} -- {{ vars.severity }}, {{ vars.process }} first seen {{ vars.first_seen }}, last seen {{ vars.last_seen }}, already carrying {{ vars.steps.Check_Existing_Exceptions.data | default([]) | length }} exception rule(s). Isolation cuts {{ vars.device }} off from the network until a "Unisolate" call releases it.

inputVariables.name: decision_note
inputVariables.label: Reason (becomes part of the alert's audit trail)
inputVariables.title: Text Area

message.content: Triage to Isolation: isolated collector {{ vars.device }} for event {{ vars.event_id }} ({{ vars.process }}, {{ vars.severity }}). Reason: {{ vars.steps.Isolation_Approval.input.decision_note }}
Triage to Isolation: isolation of {{ vars.device }} declined for event {{ vars.event_id }}. Reason: {{ vars.steps.Isolation_Approval.input.decision_note }}

groups.name: Note: Resolve Event
groups.description:
The alert's sourceId is the FortiEDR eventId (external_id the
ingestion chain maps), and the IRI is kept for the audit comments.
A slow refresh (sourceId blank -- a hand-created or foreign alert)
stops at the Missing Event step rather than calling the tenant with
a blank identifier.

groups.name: Note: Missing Event Audit
groups.description:
Either the alert is not a FortiEDR alert, or the event was pruned on
the tenant. A comment with the sourceId asks the analyst to act on
the alert's own data instead of pretending the console agrees.

groups.name: Note: Enrich
groups.description:
The fresh event row, not the ingested card, decides what the analyst
sees: severity and the collector device may both have moved since the
pull (FortiEDR correlates a re-detection into the same event and only
moves its lastSeen, so the event CAN have drifted under a static
alert card).

groups.name: Note: Collect Evidence
groups.description:
Bags the event's binary onto the alert BEFORE the approval, so
the analyst deciding on isolation has the artifacts in the same
record. Fails soft inside the child (an offline or decommissioned
collector leaves a comment, not a dead run).

groups.name: Note: Isolate Collector
groups.description:
`type: Name` + the event's collector device, the pair the tenant
answered for both isolate and unisolate. The unisolate reverse call
uses the same arguments, so releasing the endpoint later is the same
record action away through the connector operation.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Collect Evidence
workflows.description: Pulls the binary the alert fired on -- the event's process file, by its raw-event anchor -- uploads it as a FortiSOAR attachment through the connector, and links it to the alert. Degrades to a comment when the collector is offline.

arguments.record_id: {% if vars.input.params.record_id | default('', true) %} {{ vars.input.params.record_id }} {% else %} {{ vars.input.records[0]['@id'] }} {% endif %}

groups.name: Note: Resolve Inputs
groups.description:
Two entry modes share one resolve: called from a parent playbook the
explicit params win; run as a record action the alert itself carries
sourceId (the FortiEDR eventId) and the record IRI.

groups.name: Note: Bag Context
groups.description:
The file to bag is the event's own process path, plus the anchor
pieces: the raw-event repository keeps the retrieval id, and the
collector's device and the event's organization scope the call.

groups.name: Note: Bag Path Resolved
groups.description:
An event without a file path (pure log-policy events) has no
disk-evidence bag; the retrieval API needs a path to pull.

groups.name: Note: Collect File
groups.description:
Disk-mode retrieval of the event's binary, anchored to the earliest
raw item. ignore_errors: the tenant rejects the pull from an offline
or decommissioned collector, and that rejection is an outcome the
alert should record, not a reason to kill the parent triage.

groups.name: Note: Link Evidence
groups.description:
`link:` (the __link primitive the platform's own escalation uses)
APPENDS the attachment; a plain fields-write to the attachments
relationship would replace whatever the record already carried.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Allow Event (Time-Limited)
workflows.description: Record action on an ingested FortiEDR alert: creates a FortiEDR exception rule for the event with an expiry encoded in the rule's comment, and records the terms on the alert. The Exception Expiry Sweep deletes the rule when it expires.

message.content: Allow Event: no FortiEDR event found for sourceId {{ vars.event_id }}; no exception will be created.
Allow Event: refused -- event {{ vars.event_id }} already carries {{ vars.steps.Check_Existing_Exceptions.data | length }} exception rule(s). Clean them up on the console or through the sweep first.

steps.name: Expiry Form
steps.description: Creates a FortiEDR exception rule for event {{ vars.event_id }} ({{ vars.steps.Get_Event.data[0].severity }}, {{ vars.steps.Get_Event.data[0].process }}) and encodes the expiry in the rule's comment. The Exception Expiry Sweep deletes the rule once the expiry passes; without it FortiEDR keeps the rule forever.

schema.title: Time-limited exception
schema.description: Creates a FortiEDR exception rule for event {{ vars.event_id }} ({{ vars.steps.Get_Event.data[0].severity }}, {{ vars.steps.Get_Event.data[0].process }}) and encodes the expiry in the rule's comment. The Exception Expiry Sweep deletes the rule once the expiry passes; without it FortiEDR keeps the rule forever.

inputVariables.name: analyst_reason
inputVariables.label: Why this event is allowed (stored with the rule and on the alert)
inputVariables.title: Text Area

message.content: Allow Event: time-limited exception created for event {{ vars.event_id }}, expires at epoch {{ vars.expires_epoch }} ({{ vars.steps.Expiry_Form.input.expiry_days }} days). Reason: {{ vars.steps.Expiry_Form.input.analyst_reason }}. The Exception Expiry Sweep will delete the rule when it expires.
Allow Event: cancelled for event {{ vars.event_id }}; no exception was created.

groups.name: Note: Existing Exceptions
groups.description:
The event already carries at least one rule (FortiEDR keeps rules
from deleted exceptions too). A second overlapping allow is how
permanent exceptions multiply unnoticed, so this stops at the audit.

groups.name: Note: Compute Expiry
groups.description:
The marker is the sweep's whole contract:
`fortiedrv2-managed expires=<unix epoch> :: <analyst reason>`. The
sweep matches the prefix and parses the epoch; everything after the
separator is the human record. FortiEDR's own Created At field carries
only minute precision in the server's local timezone, so the epoch is
the only clock the sweep trusts.

groups.name: Note: Create Exception
groups.description:
The allow-the-event form of the create call: collector groups and
destinations open, exactly the shipped connector's semantics for
"this event qualifies everywhere". A narrower scope belongs to a
hand-built console rule, which this playbook deliberately never
guesses on the operator's behalf.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Exception Expiry Sweep
workflows.description: Deletes FortiEDR exception rules created by the Allow Event playbook whose encoded expiry has passed. Managed rules still in their window are reported and left in place; unmanaged rules are counted and never touched.

groups.name: Note: Sweep Window
groups.description:
A plain `start` (no module) is the shape the scheduled ingest
fetchers use, so this playbook drops straight into a cron entry.

groups.name: Note: List Exceptions
groups.description:
No comment filter is passed: filtering by comment on this endpoint
was not verifiably honored, and the sweep must see every rule to
count the unmanaged ones anyway. Keep the organization blank -- the
tenant then lists the configured organization, while the literal
select value "All organizations" is rejected server-side.

groups.name: Note: Find Expired
groups.description:
Defensive parse per rule: the marker prefix selects OUR rules, the
digits after it are the expiry epoch, and anything else on the
comment line is left alone. Rows without the marker are counted as
unmanaged and skipped -- the sweep must never delete a hand-built
console rule.

groups.name: Note: Delete Expired
groups.description:
Exception IDs and NOTHING else. The comment parameter on this
endpoint is a FILTER, not a note (live-observed): a delete carrying
a comment deletes only the rules whose comment matches it, so an
audit note passed as `comment` here would silently delete nothing.
The organization is omitted for the same filtering reason -- IDs
alone address the rules exactly.

groups.name: Note: Sweep Summary
groups.description:
The run's report is this step's result -- the scheduled-task view
and any parent playbook read it from here.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Re-detection Digest
workflows.description: Builds a digest task of the console incidents still absorbing re-detections, ranked by event count (the long-running compromises first) and posts it as a FortiSOAR task for the SOC queue.

groups.name: Note: Rank Incidents
groups.description:
Ranks on eventIdsNum only -- one list per incident row, integers
only, so nothing typed ever crosses the sandbox. The digest itself
is built into the snippet: row separator + inline-styled table, the
house card recipe that survives both SOAR themes.

groups.name: Note: Digest Task
groups.description:
A task is the queueable artifact on a box without a mail relay: it
lands in the SOC's task view with the digest as its description and
the operator's follow-up goes through the task's own close loop.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > IOC Retro-Hunt
workflows.description: Execute-menu action: takes a file hash, sweeps the whole FortiEDR estate for the events that harbor it, and upserts one alert per hit event (severity and device from the live event). Re-running the same hunt updates its findings without duplicating them.

inputVariables.title: File Hash
inputVariables.name: file_hash
inputVariables.tooltip: MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256 of the file to hunt for. The search covers every event the tenant still holds, the threat-hunting repository, and communicating applications.

resource.name: {{ ('FortiEDR retro-hunt: ' ~ vars.input.params.file_hash ~ ' seen on ' ~ vars.item.collectors[0].device ~ ' (' ~ vars.item.process ~ ')') | truncate(200) }}
resource.description: {{ 'Retro-hunt finding: file hash ' ~ vars.input.params.file_hash ~ ' is harbored by FortiEDR event ' ~ vars.item.eventId ~ ' on ' ~ vars.item.collectors[0].device ~ ' (' ~ vars.item.severity ~ ', ' ~ vars.item.classification ~ '), first seen ' ~ vars.item.firstSeen ~ ', last seen ' ~ vars.item.lastSeen ~ '.' }}

routes.name: Get Hunt Events -> Create Hunt Alerts

groups.name: Note: Validate Input
groups.description:
The Execute dialog requires the hash, but the API route can start
the run with a blank body -- refuse that before it reaches the
tenant.

groups.name: Note: Get Hunt Events
groups.description:
The event IDs from the hash search are fetched as one comma list,
one call: get_event_list answers with the full rows (severity,
process, the collector device) in the same shape the ingestion
pull reads.

groups.name: Note: Create Hunt Alerts
groups.description:
The same upsert contract as the ingestion chain's Create Record --
sourceId = eventId dedupes against anything the scheduled pull
already wrote -- with two deliberate differences. The name declares
itself a hunt finding, and alertDetectionDate is ABSENT from the
update set: a hunt that runs months later must not move the
incident's recorded first detection.

groups.name: Note: Hunt Summary
groups.description:
Both terminal paths land here: the finding count is zero on the no-hit
branch, and the task view shows the summary either way.

groups.name: Note: No Hash
groups.description:
A blank hash never reaches the tenant; the summary says why the run
was a no-op instead of failing with the operation's parameter
error.

workflows.name: FortiEDR v2 > Fleet Compliance Audit
workflows.description: Audits the FortiEDR collector fleet (state, recency, version vs the available installers) and files a FortiSOAR digest task. When the fleet lags behind an available installer, an approval-gated step can stage the version rollout.

resource.name: FortiEDR fleet compliance -- {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.fleet_size }} collectors, {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.outdated }} outdated, {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.not_running }} not running

steps.name: Upgrade Approval
steps.description: {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.outdated }} collector(s) run behind an available installer. Staging an update rolls the chosen version to the collector group(s) -- pick them explicitly; blank means every group. Finish prose, click approve.

schema.description: {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.outdated }} collector(s) run behind an available installer. Staging an update rolls the chosen version to the collector group(s) -- pick them explicitly; blank means every group. Finish prose, click approve.

inputVariables.name: target_version
inputVariables.label: Target version (the audit reports the latest, e.g. {{ vars.steps.Audit_Fleet.data.code_output.latest_windows }})
inputVariables.title: Text

groups.name: Note: Get Fleet
groups.description:
No organization argument: the tenant lists the connector's
configured organization when the parameter is blank, while the
literal select value "All organizations" is rejected server-side.

groups.name: Note: Get Installers
groups.description:
The installer catalogue (osFamily + version) is the reference the
outdated computation compares against. The blank organization
defaults to the configured organization server-side.

groups.name: Note: Audit Fleet
groups.description:
Pure string/int tuples only across the sandbox line. Latest-family
comparison is component-wise on the dotted version, not string
compare: 6.1.10 must rank above 6.1.9.

groups.name: Note: Staging Offered
groups.description:
The approval form appears only when the audit found something to
fix; a compliant fleet goes straight to the summary.

groups.name: Note: Map Installer
groups.description:
updateVersions is the shape the operation's schema documents: a list
of per-OS-family target rows. allow_downgrade is a real boolean on
the wire and the selection comes back as a string, so the equality
conversion happens here where the reviewer can see it.
